 ‘We play football, not cricket’: Sri Lanka coach Mutairi calls for respect ahead of Bangladesh clash
 Published : 10 November 2026
 • 
 Updated : 10 November 2026, 22:00
 • 
 FOOTBALL
 SHARE 
 Sports Reporter 
 Bangladesh players Hamza Choudhury, Sheikh Morsalin react during training on November 10, 2026. [R] Sri Lanka coach Abdullah Al Mutairi. Photo: Firoz Ahmed 
 Sri Lanka coach Abdullah Al Mutairi is expecting a high-quality contest against Bangladesh in Wednesday’s SAFF Championship encounter, but he wants the familiar cricketing rivalry between the two countries kept out of football. 
 Bangladesh have already secured a place in the semifinals and need only a draw to finish top of the group. Sri Lanka, meanwhile, must avoid defeat to advance, having been held to Sunday's 2-2 draw by Bhutan -- who lost 1-0 to the hosts.
 Tap here to add The Daily Star as a trusted source 
 Read more 'Ready to play anywhere for the team' 
 At Tuesday’s pre-match press conference, Mutairi reiterated his belief that the Group A clash at the National Stadium could be “one of the best matches in the history of the SAFF Championship”. 
 He also made clear that his side would be playing for a win, with a defeat potentially ending their campaign. “I told my players today that there is one rule in football that I believe in: win or die… We need to win or draw, but we will play for a win.” 
 Mutairi acknowledged the strength of the hosts, saying: “Both teams have quality players, whether local or of overseas origin. Bangladesh may play with less pressure, but [improving] the FIFA ranking is also important for them.” 
 Read more It's time for Bangladesh to start winning titles, says Hamza 
 The coach was also asked how his team would celebrate if they beat Bangladesh, with the question invoking the cricketing rivalry and the infamous ‘Nagin dance’ celebrations.
 “When a match ends, there is no need to celebrate in front of the other team. The most important thing is to respect others. This region already has enough problems because of cricket. People celebrate by making gestures against each other, and everyone ends up hating one another.
 Read more 'Just give Bangladesh, India the final': Sri Lanka coach Mutairi slams refereeing after Bhutan draw 
 “But we play football, not cricket. We create love. This is a competition, and we should enjoy it… Nobody dies because they lose.”
 He did, however, leave room for a little showmanship, joking that if Sri Lanka won on Wednesday, he could “dance like [Indian actor] Akshay Kumar”.
